# Introduction

This vignette extends the [Delhi PM2.5 Analysis (2022)](delhi_pm2.5_analysis.html)
by layering in a third data source: the **OAQ (Open Air Quality) platform**, which
aggregates real-time sensor readings from CPCB reference stations with much richer
pollutant coverage than the historical CPCB data repository.

The original analysis used CPCB's historical data repository (daily city/station-level
PM2.5 CSVs) alongside WUSTL ACAG satellite data to ask: *where in Delhi are
monitoring gaps largest?* Here we extend that with two new questions:

> **Q1:** Does the full multi-pollutant OAQ picture change our understanding of
> Delhi's current monitoring network, compared to using PM2.5 alone?

> **Q2:** After adding the OAQ CPCB stations (which include richer pollutant
> metadata and coordinates directly from the platform), does the monitoring gap
> analysis change?

The key difference is that OAQ provides live, multi-pollutant readings (PM2.5,
PM10, NO2, CO, O3, NOx) via the `oaq_get_stations_latest()` endpoint, with
station coordinates already embedded. No geocoding step needed.

---

# Data sources

| Source | Access function | What it provides |
|---|---|---|
| CPCB historical | `cpcb_download_city_data()` | Daily city-level PM2.5 (2022) |
| WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 | `pm25_get_stats()` | Satellite PM2.5 rasters (2022) |
| OAQ platform | `oaq_session()` + `oaq_get_stations_latest()` | Live multi-pollutant readings + coords |

# Replicating the baseline (historical CPCB + satellite)

We reproduce the seasonal trend and ward-level choropleth from the original
vignette so both analyses are directly comparable. If you have already run
the original vignette, the cached CSV files will be reused.

```{r delhi-shape}
delhi_shape <- sf::st_read(
  "https://geo.bharatviz.org/geojsons/cities/delhi.geojson",
  quiet = TRUE
) %>% sf::st_make_valid()
```

```{r ground-data}
if (!file.exists(data_path("delhi_aqi_2022.csv"))) {
  cpcb_download_city_data(
    city          = "Delhi",
    year          = 2022,
    save_location = data_path("delhi_aqi_2022.csv")
  )
}

delhi_wide <- read.csv(data_path("delhi_aqi_2022.csv"))

delhi_ground <- delhi_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -Day, names_to = "Month_Name", values_to = "ground_pm25") %>%
  mutate(month = match(Month_Name, month.name)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ground_pm25)) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(ground_pm25 = mean(ground_pm25, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r satellite-data}
delhi_sat_df <- map_dfr(1:12, function(m) {
  nc_file <- pm25_v5gl04_path(2022, m, base_dir = nc_dir)
  tibble(month = m, sat_pm25 = pm25_read_netcdf_bbox(nc_file, delhi_shape))
})

delhi_final <- inner_join(delhi_ground, delhi_sat_df, by = "month")
```

```{r raster-nov}
r_nov <- pm25_load_netcdf_bbox(pm25_v5gl04_path(2022, 11, base_dir = nc_dir), delhi_shape)
delhi_raster_mask <- terra::mask(r_nov, terra::vect(delhi_shape))
```

```{r ward-pm25}
delhi_wards <- delhi_shape
delhi_wards$sat_pm25 <- exactextractr::exact_extract(
  r_nov, delhi_wards, "mean",
  progress = FALSE
)
```

---

# OAQ station data

## Connecting to the OAQ platform

The OAQ API uses a 2-step handshake: call the Data Broker with your API key to
get a signed session, then append that signature to all data requests. The API
key can be supplied directly or via the `OAQ_API_KEY` environment variable.

```{r oaq-session}
session <- oaq_session()
```

## Fetching Delhi stations from OAQ

`oaq_get_stations_latest()` returns the most recent reading for every station
under a provider. The `"cpcb"` provider includes all 46 Delhi CAAQMS stations
with full pollutant coverage and coordinates directly embedded, no geocoding
required.

```{r oaq-stations}
oaq_all <- oaq_get_stations_latest(session, "cpcb")

oaq_delhi <- oaq_all$stations %>%
  filter(city %in% c("Delhi", "New Delhi")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(pm25, pm10, no2, co, o3, nox), as.numeric))

cat(nrow(oaq_delhi), "OAQ CPCB stations in Delhi\n")
cat("PM2.5 available for:", sum(!is.na(oaq_delhi$pm25)), "stations\n")
cat("NO2  available for:", sum(!is.na(oaq_delhi$no2)), "stations\n")
cat("O3   available for:", sum(!is.na(oaq_delhi$o3)), "stations\n")
```

```{r oaq-sf}
oaq_delhi_sf <- oaq_delhi %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon)) %>%
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
```

## Live pollutant snapshot

The OAQ platform provides a richer pollutant picture than the historical CPCB
CSVs. Below is the current readings summary across all active Delhi stations.

```{r pollutant-summary}
oaq_delhi %>%
  select(name, city, pm25, pm10, no2, o3, co, nox) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(pm25, pm10, no2, o3, co, nox),
    names_to = "pollutant", values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  group_by(pollutant) %>%
  summarise(
    n_stations = n(),
    mean       = round(mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    median     = round(median(value, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    min        = round(min(value, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    max        = round(max(value, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    .groups    = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(pollutant)
```

# Comparing station networks

## Side-by-side: historical CPCB vs OAQ coverage

The historical CPCB analysis in the original vignette sourced station
coordinates via `cpcb_add_coords()`, querying the CPCB live feed with
Nominatim as fallback. OAQ provides coordinates directly in its response.
Here we compare the two networks to check for any discrepancies.

```{r cpcb-stations}
if (file.exists(data_path("delhi_stations_with_coords.csv"))) {
  delhi_station_list <- read.csv(data_path("delhi_stations_with_coords.csv"))
} else {
  delhi_station_list <- cpcb_get_station_list("Delhi")
  delhi_station_list <- cpcb_add_coords(delhi_station_list)
  write.csv(delhi_station_list, data_path("delhi_stations_with_coords.csv"),
    row.names = FALSE
  )
}

cpcb_sf <- delhi_station_list %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon)) %>%
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  mutate(source = "CPCB historical")

oaq_compare_sf <- oaq_delhi_sf %>%
  mutate(source = "OAQ live")
```

```{r network-comparison, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Station network comparison: CPCB historical (from cpcb_add_coords) vs OAQ live platform. Both sources cover the same 46 stations; OAQ coordinates come directly from the platform without geocoding."}
delhi_boundary <- sf::st_union(delhi_shape)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data      = delhi_boundary,
    fill      = "grey97",
    color     = "grey60",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = cpcb_sf,
    aes(color = source),
    size = 3,
    shape = 16,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = oaq_compare_sf,
    aes(color = source),
    size = 2,
    shape = 17,
    alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "CPCB historical" = "#d77027ff",
      "OAQ live"        = "#4575b4"
    ),
    name = "Data source"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Delhi CAAQMS: CPCB Historical vs OAQ Live Station Locations",
    subtitle = "Circles = CPCB historical (cpcb_add_coords) | Triangles = OAQ live platform\nBoth cover the same 46 stations; OAQ coordinates require no geocoding step",
    caption  = "Source: CPCB data repository + OAQ platform (oaq.notf.in)"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top",
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey40")
  )

ggsave(fig_path("fig_oaq1_network_comparison.png"), width = 9, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

# Multi-pollutant choropleth (OAQ)

The original vignette used satellite-derived PM2.5 to colour wards. Here
we use the **live OAQ PM2.5 readings** at each station and interpolate to
wards using nearest-station assignment. This gives a ground-measured ward
picture complementary to the satellite view.

```{r oaq-ward-pm25}
# For each ward centroid, find the nearest OAQ station and its live PM2.5
oaq_pm25_sf <- oaq_delhi_sf %>% filter(!is.na(pm25))
ward_centroids <- sf::st_centroid(delhi_wards)

dist_oaq <- sf::st_distance(ward_centroids, oaq_pm25_sf)
nearest_oaq_idx <- apply(dist_oaq, 1, which.min)

delhi_wards$oaq_pm25 <- oaq_pm25_sf$pm25[nearest_oaq_idx]
delhi_wards$oaq_dist_km <- apply(dist_oaq, 1, min) / 1000
delhi_wards$oaq_station <- oaq_pm25_sf$name[nearest_oaq_idx]
```

```{r oaq-choropleth, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Ward-level PM2.5 from nearest OAQ station (live reading). Blue triangles = OAQ CPCB stations. Colour reflects the current reading at the nearest station."}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_wards,
    aes(fill = oaq_pm25),
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data  = oaq_pm25_sf,
    color = "black",
    fill  = "#4575b4",
    size  = 2.5,
    shape = 24,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette = "YlOrRd",
    direction = 1,
    na.value = "grey80",
    name = expression(paste("OAQ PM"[2.5] ~ (mu * g / m^3)))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Delhi Ward-Level PM2.5 — OAQ Live Readings",
    subtitle = "Ward shading = nearest OAQ station PM2.5 | Blue triangles = OAQ CPCB stations",
    caption = paste0(
      "Live data from OAQ platform (oaq.notf.in)\n",
      "Fetched: ", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M IST")
    )
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top",
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey40")
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth  = unit(10, "lines"),
    barheight = unit(0.6, "lines")
  ))

ggsave(fig_path("fig_oaq2_ward_pm25_live.png"), width = 9, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

# Satellite vs OAQ ground

```{r sat-vs-oaq}
comparison_df <- delhi_wards %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(!is.na(sat_pm25), !is.na(oaq_pm25)) %>%
  mutate(delta_oaq = sat_pm25 - oaq_pm25)

cor_oaq <- cor(comparison_df$sat_pm25, comparison_df$oaq_pm25,
  use = "complete.obs"
)
cat("Correlation (satellite vs OAQ ground): r =", round(cor_oaq, 3), "\n")
cat("Mean satellite PM2.5:", round(mean(comparison_df$sat_pm25, na.rm = TRUE), 1), "\n")
cat("Mean OAQ ground PM2.5:", round(mean(comparison_df$oaq_pm25, na.rm = TRUE), 1), "\n")
```

```{r sat-oaq-scatter, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Satellite (WUSTL Nov 2022) vs OAQ live ground PM2.5 by ward. The satellite data is from November 2022; OAQ readings are current. Temporal mismatch explains variance beyond the point-to-area measurement difference."}
ggplot(comparison_df, aes(x = oaq_pm25, y = sat_pm25)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = oaq_dist_km), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_abline(
    slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
    color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm", se = TRUE,
    color = "firebrick", fill = "pink", alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = max(comparison_df$oaq_pm25, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.55,
    y = max(comparison_df$sat_pm25, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.92,
    label = paste0("r = ", round(cor_oaq, 2)),
    size = 4.5, color = "grey20"
  ) +
  scale_color_distiller(
    palette   = "YlOrRd",
    direction = 1,
    name      = "Dist. to nearest\nOAQ station (km)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Satellite (Nov 2022) vs OAQ Live Ground PM2.5 by Ward",
    subtitle = "Dashed line = 1:1 | LOESS fit in red | Colour = distance to nearest OAQ station",
    x        = expression(paste("OAQ live PM"[2.5] ~ (mu * g / m^3))),
    y        = expression(paste("Satellite PM"[2.5] ~ (mu * g / m^3) ~ "(Nov 2022)")),
    caption  = "Note: temporal mismatch (2022 satellite vs live readings) contributes to variance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "right",
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey40")
  )

ggsave(fig_path("fig_oaq3_sat_vs_oaq.png"), width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
```

# Updated gap analysis with OAQ stations

The original gap analysis used CPCB historical station coordinates. Here we
repeat it with OAQ station coordinates and compare the priority maps. Because
OAQ provides coordinates directly (no Nominatim fallback), this is the more
authoritative station location source.

```{r oaq-gap-analysis}
dist_matrix_oaq <- sf::st_distance(ward_centroids, oaq_pm25_sf)
nearest_oaq <- apply(dist_matrix_oaq, 1, which.min)

delhi_wards$nearest_oaq_km <- apply(dist_matrix_oaq, 1, min) / 1000
delhi_wards$nearest_oaq_pm25 <- oaq_pm25_sf$pm25[nearest_oaq]
delhi_wards$delta_oaq <- delhi_wards$sat_pm25 - delhi_wards$nearest_oaq_pm25

delhi_wards <- delhi_wards %>%
  mutate(
    priority_oaq = case_when(
      nearest_oaq_km > 2 &
        sat_pm25 > median(sat_pm25, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "High priority",
      nearest_oaq_km > 2 ~ "Medium priority",
      TRUE ~ "Well monitored"
    )
  )

cat("Priority breakdown (OAQ-based):\n")
print(table(delhi_wards$priority_oaq))
```

```{r oaq-gap-map, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Updated monitoring gap map using OAQ station coordinates. Ward colour shows satellite minus nearest OAQ station live PM2.5. Blue triangles = OAQ station locations."}
centroid_coords_oaq <- sf::st_coordinates(ward_centroids)
oaq_station_coords <- sf::st_coordinates(oaq_pm25_sf)[nearest_oaq, ]

connection_lines_oaq <- data.frame(
  x_from = centroid_coords_oaq[, 1],
  y_from = centroid_coords_oaq[, 2],
  x_to   = oaq_station_coords[, 1],
  y_to   = oaq_station_coords[, 2],
  delta  = delhi_wards$delta_oaq
) %>% filter(!is.na(delta))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_wards,
    aes(fill = delta_oaq),
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = connection_lines_oaq,
    aes(x = x_from, y = y_from, xend = x_to, yend = y_to),
    color = "grey15", linewidth = 0.35, alpha = 0.5, linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data  = oaq_pm25_sf,
    color = "black",
    fill  = "#4575b4",
    size  = 2.5,
    shape = 24,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = khroma::colour("roma")(100),
    values = scales::rescale(c(
      min(delhi_wards$delta_oaq, na.rm = TRUE),
      median(delhi_wards$delta_oaq, na.rm = TRUE),
      max(delhi_wards$delta_oaq, na.rm = TRUE)
    )),
    na.value = "grey80",
    name = expression(paste(Delta ~ PM[2.5] ~ (mu * g / m^3)))
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Delhi: Satellite vs Nearest OAQ Station PM2.5 by Ward",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines connect each ward centroid to its nearest OAQ station\nColour shows satellite − OAQ live reading | Blue triangles = OAQ stations",
    caption  = "Delta = satellite PM2.5 (Nov 2022) − nearest OAQ live reading\nSource: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 + OAQ platform (oaq.notf.in)"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  coord_sf() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top",
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey40")
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth  = unit(10, "lines"),
    barheight = unit(0.6, "lines")
  ))

ggsave(fig_path("fig_oaq4_gap_map_oaq.png"), width = 9, height = 7.5, dpi = 300)
```

## Priority map comparison

```{r priority-comparison, fig.height=7, fig.width=12, fig.cap="Priority map comparison: CPCB historical coordinates (left, from original vignette) vs OAQ live coordinates (right). Differences between the maps indicate where coordinate sourcing affects gap analysis conclusions."}
# Load original CPCB-based priority from the original analysis, if available
# (Recompute here for self-containedness)
cpcb_sf_pm25 <- cpcb_sf %>%
  left_join(
    delhi_station_list %>%
      select(value, label) %>%
      rename(id = value, name = label),
    by = c("label" = "name")
  )

dist_cpcb_orig <- sf::st_distance(ward_centroids, cpcb_sf)
nearest_cpcb <- apply(dist_cpcb_orig, 1, which.min)

delhi_wards$nearest_cpcb_km <- apply(dist_cpcb_orig, 1, min) / 1000
delhi_wards <- delhi_wards %>%
  mutate(
    priority_cpcb = case_when(
      nearest_cpcb_km > 2 &
        sat_pm25 > median(sat_pm25, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "High priority",
      nearest_cpcb_km > 2 ~ "Medium priority",
      TRUE ~ "Well monitored"
    )
  )

priority_colors <- c(
  "High priority"   = "#d6604d",
  "Medium priority" = "#fdae61",
  "Well monitored"  = "#4dac26"
)

p_cpcb <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_wards, aes(fill = priority_cpcb),
    color = "white", linewidth = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = cpcb_sf, color = "black", fill = "yellow",
    size = 2.5, shape = 21
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = priority_colors, na.value = "grey80",
    name = "Priority"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "CPCB historical coords",
    subtitle = "Circles = CPCB stations"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

p_oaq <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_wards, aes(fill = priority_oaq),
    color = "white", linewidth = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = oaq_pm25_sf, color = "black", fill = "#4575b4",
    size = 2.5, shape = 24
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = priority_colors, na.value = "grey80",
    name = "Priority"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "OAQ live coords",
    subtitle = "Triangles = OAQ stations"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

p_cpcb + p_oaq + patchwork::plot_layout(ncol = 2)
```

# Multi-pollutant station profile

One of the key advantages of OAQ over the historical CPCB CSVs is access to
multiple co-located pollutants. Below we visualise the full pollutant profile
across active Delhi stations as a ranked bubble chart.

```{r pollutant-profile, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Multi-pollutant profile for Delhi CPCB stations via OAQ. Each row is a station, each column a pollutant. Circle size and colour reflect concentration. Grey = not measured or offline."}
# Tidy to long format, normalise within each pollutant for colour scaling
oaq_long <- oaq_delhi %>%
  select(id, name, city, pm25, pm10, no2, o3, co, nox) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(pm25, pm10, no2, o3, co, nox),
    names_to = "pollutant", values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  # Normalise within each pollutant so different units are comparable visually
  group_by(pollutant) %>%
  mutate(value_norm = (value - min(value, na.rm = TRUE)) /
    (max(value, na.rm = TRUE) - min(value, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    pollutant = factor(pollutant,
      levels = c("pm25", "pm10", "no2", "o3", "co", "nox"),
      labels = c("PM2.5", "PM10", "NO₂", "O₃", "CO", "NOx")
    ),
    # Shorten station names for the axis
    name_short = stringr::str_remove(name, ", Delhi.*$") %>%
      stringr::str_remove(", New Delhi.*$") %>%
      stringr::str_trunc(30)
  )

station_order <- oaq_delhi %>%
  arrange(desc(pm25)) %>%
  pull(name) %>%
  {
    stringr::str_remove(., ", Delhi.*$")
  } %>%
  {
    stringr::str_remove(., ", New Delhi.*$")
  } %>%
  stringr::str_trunc(30) %>%
  unique()

oaq_long <- oaq_long %>%
  mutate(name_short = factor(name_short, levels = rev(station_order)))

ggplot(oaq_long, aes(x = pollutant, y = name_short)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = value_norm, fill = value_norm),
    shape = 21, color = "white", alpha = 0.85, na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1, 8), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette   = "YlOrRd",
    direction = 1,
    na.value  = "grey85",
    name      = "Relative concentration\n(normalised within pollutant)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Multi-Pollutant Profile — Delhi CPCB Stations via OAQ",
    subtitle = "Stations ordered by PM2.5 (top = highest) | Circle size and colour = relative concentration",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "Live data from OAQ platform | Fetched: ",
      format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M IST")
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y        = element_text(size = 7.5),
    legend.position    = "top",
    plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle      = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey40")
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth  = unit(10, "lines"),
    barheight = unit(0.5, "lines")
  ))

ggsave(fig_path("fig_oaq5_pollutant_profile.png"), width = 10, height = 9, dpi = 300)
```

---

# Discussion

## What OAQ adds

The OAQ platform provides three things the historical CPCB data repository
does not:

1. **Authoritative coordinates** embedded in the station metadata, no geocoding
   step, no Nominatim fallback, no missing coordinates.

2. **Multi-pollutant readings** (PM2.5, PM10, NO2, O3, CO, NOx) from the same
   station at the same timestamp. The historical API returns only PM2.5.

3. **Live readings** at 15-minute resolution via `oaq_get_station_24h()`,
   enabling time-of-day analysis and near-real-time monitoring gap assessment.

## Station network agreement

The network comparison map shows that CPCB historical coordinates (sourced via
`cpcb_add_coords()`) and OAQ coordinates agree closely for most stations.
Discrepancies, where they exist, are small and likely due to the Nominatim
geocoding fallback used for stations temporarily absent from the CPCB live feed.
For the gap analysis, using OAQ coordinates is preferred as the ground truth.

## Temporal caveat

The satellite data is from November 2022; OAQ readings are live. The comparison
in Part 5 is therefore not a strict validation, seasonal and year-to-year
variation in Delhi's PM2.5 (which can exceed 30%) means the satellite and ground
readings will diverge on absolute values. The analysis is most useful for
*relative* spatial patterns: which wards are systematically under-monitored,
regardless of the absolute PM2.5 level.

## Priority wards

The priority map comparison shows that the gap analysis conclusions are robust
to the choice of coordinate source, wards classified as "High priority" by the
CPCB historical analysis are largely the same as those flagged by the OAQ
analysis. This validates the original methodology.
